name: Longdawn
description: Longdawn keeps one face forever turned toward its dim orange sun, and the result is a world of a single frozen sunset: the star sits eternally just above the horizon, smearing the ice in bands of rose, copper, and violet. Behind you, the night hemisphere rises in glaciers tall enough to have weather patterns of their own. At the subsolar point, a shallow sea of meltwater steams gently under that never-setting light.

The world is nearly silent—wind is scarce in the thin atmosphere, so sound dies within meters. What reaches you is the creak of settling ice, kilometers thick, and occasionally a deep subglacial groan from the ocean below as tides flex the crust. The air smells of nothing at all until you near the melt sea, where it carries a faint mineral tang, like struck flint.

The colony ship Kestrel's Dawn came down hard on the twilight slope ninety years ago, its hull now a cathedral of frost half-swallowed by a crevasse, and its escape pods are strewn across forty kilometers of methane lake ice like dropped seeds. Officially there were no survivors; unofficially, someone maintained a distress beacon for eleven years after the crash. The crystal caverns beneath the wreck hold carvings no registered colonist has claimed.

Beneath all that ice lies a liquid ocean warmed by tidal kneading, and in the melt sea's shallows live the only known life: rust-colored microbial mats, thriving nowhere else, already retreating as the melt zone shrinks decade by decade. Xenobiologists want samples before the mats vanish; salvagers want the Kestrel's black box, which recorded something during descent it should not have seen. The ice gives up neither easily.
